headline: 640 V cascade record
parameters: 5000 fps; ≈55 ms window; four successive detached episodes
description: Cascade in which the mother drop sheds successive daughters; each episode re-forms a neck at the apex before the next breakup.

headline: 600 V, first-extension record
description: High-speed record of the first spreading excursion at 600 V, resolved frame by frame around the pinch-off event.

headline: 550 V pinch-off record
parameters: 2000 fps; 100 ms window; pinch-off at 8.5 ms
description: Reference pinch-off case: the daughter detaches at ≈8.5 ms and is subsequently partially reabsorbed.

headline: 100 V record
description: Sub-threshold voltage: the drop spreads only slightly and no neck forms.

headline: 200 V record
description: Intermediate voltage; no interface breakup within the recorded window.

headline: 300 V record
description: Intermediate voltage; the apex deforms but recoils without breakup.

headline: 400 V record
description: Intermediate voltage; conical neck develops and then relaxes.

headline: 500 V record
description: High voltage but still below the dynamical threshold: a conical neck forms and is withdrawn without satellite formation.

headline: 600 V pinch-off record
description: Same physical case as S02 at full record length, used for the quantitative neck-angle and extension-ratio measurements.

headline: Experiment vs simulation, event-aligned
parameters: left: 550 V experiment; right: simulation, θE = 60°; Δt = −6.0 to +5.0 ms, 0.5 ms steps
description: Side-by-side sequence aligned on the pinch-off instant, used in Note S12 and Figure S7 to show that the two neck histories coincide in time as well as in shape.

headline: Simulation, θE = 27°
description: Deep spreading limit; the computed interface pinches off early and the daughter stays detached to the end of the window.

headline: Simulation, θE = 35°
description: Second separation observed at ≈20.8 ms; the secondary daughter is partly reabsorbed at ≈21.6 ms.

headline: Simulation, θE = 40°
description: Pinch-off followed by complete reabsorption of the daughter within the window.

headline: Simulation, θE = 45° (baseline)
description: Baseline case used for the viscosity and drop-size scans (S16–S21).

headline: Simulation, θE = 50°
description: Marginal pinch-off: the daughter forms and is then pulled back.

headline: Simulation, θE = 55°
description: Secondary daughter appears at ≈16 ms and hovers for ≈43.5 ms before merging.

headline: Simulation, drop size 0.50
description: Smallest drop of the size scan; the pinch-off time scales as s^1.5.

headline: Simulation, drop size 1.65
description: Intermediate drop size of the scan.

headline: Simulation, drop size 2.50
description: Largest drop of the scan; the daughter is still ejected.

headline: Simulation, oil viscosity ×0.5
description: Thinner ambient oil; the neck still pinches off.

headline: Simulation, oil viscosity ×2
description: Moderately damped case, still above the suppression threshold.

headline: Simulation, oil viscosity ×10
description: Viscous suppression: the same neck geometry is withdrawn, and no daughter forms.
